www.pluralinvesting.com | chris.waller@pluralinvesting.com | 3 
Despite the company’s continued growth, WOSG shares declined by 15% in 2025. We believe that investors underappreciate the quality of WOSG’s business and that its economics more closely resemble a subsidiary of Rolex than a typical retailer. A key reason for the company’s economics is the lengthy waiting lists for most Rolex watches, which results in almost guaranteed sales and significant pricing power. While waiting lists have reduced since their peak in 2022, our data suggests they remain very healthy and stopped declining in the US roughly 18 months ago. Our investment thesis in WOSG is not based on tariffs or short-term macro fluctuations, but instead that the US offers a large market for the company to deploy capital at 20% returns. That thesis continued to play out last year. We estimate that WOSG’s share of Rolex stores in the US increased from 7% to 9%, while its share of sales is higher because it owns several flagship stores that are much larger than the average store. Another opportunity for WOSG to gain share is to buy stores run by mom & pops who are unable or unwilling to invest the million(s) of dollars required to refurbish stores up to Rolex’s standards. Principles of Our Partnership I take the trust you place in me very seriously and view this as a partnership. These principles are inspired by a similar letter Warren Buffett wrote in 1962 to his partners at the beginning of their partnership. They are my attempt to be up-front about what I can and cannot promise you, and what I ask from you in return: 1. Success for the fund in five years’ time is delivering a substantially higher return than global stock market indices, rather than how many clients or assets are under management. The investment approach and my time are allocated accordingly. 2. I cannot guarantee that the fund will achieve this success. However, I can promise that the vast majority of my liquid net worth will be invested alongside you. 3. The fund will only invest in businesses that I estimate are worth substantially more than the price they are trading at. 4.
